question: What does viewing a patient in their social context primarily involve?

options.A: Isolating the patient from family members during treatment
options.B: Recognizing how relationships and living conditions affect health
options.C: Focusing strictly on the diseased organ and laboratory values
options.D: Prioritizing hospital policies over community traditions

explanation: Social context looks at the broader picture of a person's life, including family and living conditions, which deeply influence health outcomes. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why might a clinically successful hospital treatment fail once the patient goes home?

options.A: Hospital laboratories are always more accurate than home testing
options.B: The patient's home environment and social support were ignored
options.C: Doctors usually prescribe the wrong medications for home use
options.D: Nurses fail to document the discharge date properly

explanation: If a care plan does not fit a patient's real-life social and financial situation at home, they will struggle to follow it. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: According to family systems theory, what happens when one family member falls seriously ill?

options.A: Daily household routines remain entirely unchanged
options.B: Family income automatically increases to cover treatment
options.C: The balance of the entire household is disrupted
options.D: The other members become completely immune to the disease

explanation: Because family members are closely linked, an illness in one person creates a ripple effect that impacts everyone in the home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: A father is admitted for chronic hypertension. Why should the nurse involve his spouse and children in his discharge education?

options.A: Family members must take over the patient's job responsibilities
options.B: Hospital regulations require at least three visitors per patient
options.C: It prevents the patient from speaking to the doctor alone
options.D: The family functions as a unit, and lifestyle changes require household support

explanation: Diet and lifestyle changes are much easier to maintain when the whole family understands and participates in them. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which family structure typically has a wide pool of available caregivers living close by?
explanation: Extended families include grandparents and other relatives who can easily share caregiving duties and emotional support. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a common health vulnerability frequently faced by single-parent households?

options.A: High financial strain and limited time for healthcare appointments
options.B: Too many conflicting medical opinions from relatives
options.C: Total immunity to common childhood infectious diseases
options.D: Excessive living space leading to social isolation

explanation: Single parents often carry the entire financial and domestic burden alone, making it hard to prioritize routine health visits. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a common result when a primary breadwinner develops a disabling chronic illness?

options.A: Automatic government provision of permanent housing
options.B: The complete elimination of domestic chores
options.C: Shifts in household roles and financial responsibilities
options.D: Immediate improvement in overall family communication

explanation: A major illness forces other family members to take over tasks previously managed by the sick individual. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: An adolescent daughter tells the nurse she is exhausted from missing school to look after her sick mother. What should the nurse recognize?

options.A: The family is experiencing role strain and needs additional support
options.B: The teenager is simply misbehaving and needs stricter discipline
options.C: The mother's illness has cured itself through natural rest
options.D: Normal adolescent development includes full-time caregiving

explanation: When children take on heavy caregiving roles, it signals that the family system is strained and requires outside intervention. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following is a primary way the community environment influences health?

options.A: Replacing the need for individual personal hygiene
options.B: Providing access to safe water, markets, and local clinics
options.C: Ensuring every citizen has a high-paying professional job
options.D: Eliminating all infectious diseases from the environment

explanation: Basic community infrastructure like clean water and nearby health clinics directly dictates physical well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: How can community cultural norms impact how people seek medical care?

options.A: They force doctors to change scientific medical facts
options.B: They can either encourage early treatment or promote harmful myths
options.C: They automatically guarantee high hospital attendance rates
options.D: They have zero effect on modern medical treatment choices

explanation: Beliefs shared within a community strongly influence whether people trust modern healthcare or rely solely on unproven remedies. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of using a genogram during a family nursing assessment?

options.A: To calculate the exact monthly income of the household
options.B: To track the daily caloric intake of the patient
options.C: To list all community parks near the patient's home
options.D: To map out inherited medical conditions across generations

explanation: A genogram acts as a detailed family tree that helps nurses identify hereditary health risks and family patterns. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is it important to include the family when creating a patient's care plan?

options.A: It legally forces the family to pay all hospital bills
options.B: It ensures the plan fits their routine and improves cooperation
options.C: It stops the doctor from making any changes to the treatment
options.D: It reduces the total number of nursing shifts required

explanation: When families help build the plan, they understand it better and are much more likely to help carry it out at home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is a primary role of a public health nurse in the community?

options.A: Connecting families to local health and social support resources
options.B: Writing national health policies for pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Managing the financial budgets of local government hospitals
options.D: Performing complex major surgeries in community centers

explanation: Public health nurses link individuals and families to clinics, support groups, and welfare services that promote wellbeing. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h7)

question: A discharged mother struggles to afford nutritious food for her infant. Which action by the nurse best shows community-focused care?

options.A: Advising her to stop feeding the infant until she finds a better job
options.B: Referring the mother to a local community food program or welfare service
options.C: Keeping the infant admitted in the acute hospital ward indefinitely
options.D: Telling her to buy more expensive imported baby formula immediately

explanation: Connecting the family to local community assistance helps solve the root social cause of their nutritional challenge. You're being a true advocate!
